demos.heading: Before you run anything: set up the shell
demos.purpose: DocuMind can answer a tenant's questions from four stores: its own Vector Search index (the ANN tier), the Firestore rung beneath it, or two managed mirrors, Vertex AI RAG Engine and Vertex AI Search. make up pins acme to RAG Engine and zeta to Vertex AI Search so every store the course teaches is exercised. A managed store holds the text of every current version, but not the kit's addresses: its citations come back with ids like acme:acme_497809ff...#rag-532341da71fe, a page of null even for a PDF, and stages.retrieval_backend: rag_engine. This lesson is about the kit's own rows, so point acme at them for the duration and put the pin back at the end. Module 2 compares the four stores; Module 7 studies the mirrors. The shell, in the kit, with PROJECT, REGION, NUMBER, API and tok from the block above. Steps 4 to 7 run offline at Rs 0 and need no project. Their Python cells need only the shell's own Python; the first make agent-turn or make agent-eval builds ~/graph-venv with the chat image's pins (lessons 5.4, 10.1 and 10.2 may have made it already), which takes a few minutes once. Step 3 uses the chat service on your lane; steps 8 and 9 call gemini-3.6-flash on location global, and rag-api's /v1/passages as documind-ui-sa. The bench's desk searches by class and drops every passage that has none (services/chat/desk_agent.py, _search()). Lesson 10.1's setup line gave acme's and zeta's stored rows their classes. If you have not run it, run this now: the 12 rows are acme's but one, zeta's carry-forward. A second run finds nothing to change. An exit status of 3 means BigQuery deferred a statement, and its last line says to run it again later.

demos.heading: The figure check on its own, at Rs 0
demos.purpose: agent_patterns.py imports only the standard library and the kit's shared/ at the top, so the shell's own Python runs the check. The cell works the gratuity row's figure out with desk_calc.calculate(), uses the Code's own words as quoted in desk_calc.RULES as the passage, and puts eight answers through figure_check(). Then it asks check_args about a wage the question does not state, once on the person's question and once with a note's words put into it. After a failed check, ask_reflect() writes the reflect call's user turn: the question, the answer, what the attempt did (did_lines()) and the verdict. cut_note() turns its reply into the note, and noted() puts every note into the next attempt's system prompt. The cell gives ask_reflect() an attempt whose calculator returned Rs 2,40,000 and whose answer wrote Rs 2,50,000, then cuts a long reply the way verify cuts every note.

By the kit's own count the turn costs about Rs 1.16 before thinking when its first attempt passes, and each retry adds about Rs 1.31; step 10 shows how that count is made.
